records.summary: A palm-sized rolling camera with a 2K, 137° lens that an owner drives around the house from the Enabot app, talking through it and playing with a pet using its laser pointer, before it drives back to its dock to recharge.
records.fit: Suits pet owners who want to look into more than one room without mounting cameras, on hard floors or low-pile carpet. Those who want scheduled patrols, two-way video or a robot that follows a pet need the EBO Air 2 Plus ($319 on Enabot's store), and a fixed pan-tilt camera such as the Petcube Cam 360 ($46.99) costs far less if one room is enough.
caveats: The Irish Times' Ciara O'Brien (June 2025) found it occasionally got trapped and ran flat, returned to its dock only most of the time, dropped Wi-Fi in parts of a mesh-networked house and may struggle on deep-pile carpet.
Her cat refused to interact with it, and Digital Camera World's Adam Waring (June 2025) had to bribe his cat with treats; he also found the app not intuitive and the preset actions fiddly.
It is not autonomous: there is no scheduled patrol on the Air 2, and video is one-way (Enabot FAQ).
Battery runs 4–7 hours, and it climbs only 4° slopes and 6 mm obstacles (Enabot).
$139 is Enabot's Black Friday price (Nov 19–30) against $199; Enabot offers 30-day price protection on sale orders.

records.summary: Enabot's step-up robot camera: a 3K rolling camera that maps the home, runs scheduled patrols, follows a person or pet, and makes two-way video calls on its eye screens. It docks itself to recharge and records to an included 32 GB card.
records.fit: Suits households that want a mobile security camera and a video-call stand-in for family, with checking on pets as one use among several. caveats: No laser pointer, unlike the cheaper EBO Air 2 (Enabot FAQ).

records.summary: A self-righting rolling pet camera with a 2K lens and a 5,000 mAh battery that Enabot rates for up to 25 days between charges, driven by hand from the app with two-way audio. It has no dock, laser or patrol mode, which is how it gets that battery life.
records.fit: Suits pet owners who are away for days at a time and want to roll around the home to check on a pet, with no dock to place. Those who want the robot to recharge itself and play laser chase should take the EBO Air 2 ($139 on Enabot's store).
caveats: No charging dock or automatic recharging: it has to be picked up and charged by cable (Enabot FAQ).
No laser pointer, no patrol mode, and the eye lights cannot be customized (Enabot FAQ).
Enabot does not say what use the 25-day battery figure assumes; The AU Review's Shantelle Santos (March 2025) got about three weeks before the first charge.
The AU Review found it got stuck in front of raised surfaces a few times, and her dogs knocked it over, though it proved sturdy.
Enabot's own spec and comparison tables disagree on climbing slope (15° vs 6°) and noise (55 vs 48.5 dB).
Enabot sells only an 'International Version' and also lists a 'ROLA Mini FamilyBot' at the same $129.99 without stating a difference. $129.99 is the Black Friday price (Nov 19–30) against $169.
